summary:
Patient Overview
Eehab Saadat, a 23-year-old intersex patient, presents with mild persistent asthma with environmental trigger sensitivity. Recent spirometry results show reduced FEV1 (68% predicted) and FEV1/FVC ratio (0.65) consistent with obstructive airway disease.

Key Findings
• Spirometry (2025-10-28) shows reduced FEV1 and FEV1/FVC ratio consistent with obstructive airway disease
• Elevated IgE (240 IU/mL) and eosinophils (8%) support allergic asthma diagnosis
• Chest X-ray (2025-10-28) shows possible mild hyperinflation with no consolidation or acute infiltrates
• CBC (2025-10-28) within normal limits with appropriate differential count
• SpO2 mildly reduced at 92% on room air

Risk Assessment
Moderate risk for asthma exacerbation, particularly during smog season or cold weather. Patient demonstrates environmental trigger sensitivity and requires consistent maintenance therapy. BMI of 30 indicates obesity which may contribute to respiratory symptoms. Recommend close monitoring during high pollution periods and regular spirometry follow-ups.

Recommendations
• Continue beclometasone dipropionate inhaler (50 mcg) twice daily for maintenance
• Keep rescue inhaler (short-acting beta-agonist) accessible for acute episodes
• Avoid exposure to smog, smoke, dust, and pollen triggers
• Consider weight management program to improve respiratory function
• Follow up with pulmonologist every 3 months for spirometry monitoring
• Use air purifiers indoors during pollution season
• Maintain diltiazem and apixaban therapy as prescribed for cardiac rate control
